scope: Proof-only checked records use explicit empty carriers, nullary checked constructors and proof-erased results without collapsing into absence or Unit.

edits.current:
A checked record with no runtime fields is rendered as a single-case enum, for
example `enum witness { empty }`, and a `Unit` field as `enum { unit }`. That is
the generator's WIT representation of an empty carrier, not a distinction in the
Lean type; such a value stays distinct from `option<witness>` and from any
absent or default value.

For a record whose proofs relate its fields, use a [checked constructor over the payload fields](existing-package.md#export-a-record-with-proof-fields). The host supplies no proof. The compiler checks each input through the selected Lean constructor and erases proofs from Lean-produced results. Closed `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String` indices stay in authenticated type metadata and never become host fields; the [complete hosted value-index matrix](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-matrix-promotion-20261020.md) exercises all three closed forms at top-level copied checked-record parameters and results in all 17 consumer profiles. Top-level inputs and results have installed acceptance in C/C++, Node JavaScript/TypeScript, browser pages, React, workers, Python, Rust, Ruby, .NET, Java/Kotlin, Perl, native PHP, PHP-Wasm and WIT/WASI. npm has [installed nested acceptance](../evidence/nested-checked-record-browser-20261016/index.json), C/C++ have an [installed nested archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-native-20261016/index.json), .NET has an [installed NuGet archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-dotnet-20261016/index.json), Java/Kotlin have an [installed Maven archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-jvm-20261016/index.json), Perl has an [installed CPAN archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-perl-20261016/index.json), native PHP has an [installed Composer archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-20261016/index.json), Python has an [installed wheel archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-python-20261016/index.json), Ruby has an [installed gem archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-ruby-20261016/index.json), WIT/WASI has an [installed component archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-wit-20261016/index.json), PHP-Wasm has an [installed Node/Chromium archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-wasm-20261016/index.json), and Rust has an [installed Cargo archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-rust-20261016/index.json). They cover direct and repeated parameters, arrays, lists, options, products, `Except`/`Result`, enclosing record fields, active variant fields and constructor-free container results. [Installed inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) additionally covers the tested acyclic `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain, with independently selected parent and child constructors and proof-free results. Select the record constructor and each nested checked field's constructor independently at every public input site; only an active variant branch runs. A record whose only fields are proofs is still a checked record: declare it with an explicit `: Type`, select a nullary constructor such as `def mkWitness : Option Witness`, and the host passes and receives an empty carrier that is distinct from an absent, null or default value; a record with one `Unit` field beside its proofs keeps that field. Generic or recursive checked records, value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, callback, owned and open dependent combinations remain unfinished.
